[ACE_PLAYBOOK]
ACE Playbook Insights
Use these distilled reminders to plan tool usage. Keep tool calls faithful to the functions provided in the BFCL benchmark.

trading_bot
- delta1: When user asks to review orders, call get_order_history first to retrieve available orders
- delta10: Execute cancel_order using available order IDs from context - never require explicit order ID when inferable from conversation
- delta11: delta11: Avoid redundant watchlist checks when not explicitly requested - execute watchlist operations directly without pre-validation
- delta12: Execute core trading operations directly - never call get_stock_info or get_account_info for validation unless explicitly requested
- delta13: Maintain state integrity by avoiding extra tool calls and conversational text that alter internal state beyond requested operations
- delta14: Execute get_symbol_by_name once per company name - avoid redundant symbol lookups in same conversation
- delta15: Avoid trading_get_login_status entirely - execute trading operations directly without authentication checks, even when login state appears ambiguous
- delta16: Avoid get_stock_info for price validation when placing orders - execute place_order directly with available parameters
- delta17: Call get_account_info before withdraw_funds to verify account status and balance - never assume sufficient funds from context
- delta18: Execute pending operations across turns without interruption - avoid explanatory text, system commentary, or function availability claims between operations
- delta19: Continue watchlist operations immediately after symbol resolution - never insert explanatory text between lookup and execution
- delta2: Only call get_order_details for specific order IDs when explicitly provided by user
- delta20: Always output structured response lists in multi-turn conversations - never omit response list format even when no tool calls are needed
- delta21: Never claim tool unavailability then execute it - maintain consistent function access assumptions across all turns, especially when user input appears ambiguous
- delta22: Execute add_to_watchlist immediately when company name is provided - avoid conversational interruptions requesting symbol validation
- delta23: Avoid get_stock_info for market analysis when user requests order placement - execute place_order directly with available parameters
- delta24: Execute add_to_watchlist immediately in first turn when company name provided - avoid conversational interruptions requesting symbols
- delta25: Maintain structured response list format across all turns - conversational text alone triggers inference errors
- delta26: Execute cancel_order automatically when order history reveals pending orders - never require explicit confirmation for inferable cancellations
- delta27: Avoid get_stock_info calls for invalid symbols - execute only requested operations without speculative validation
- delta28: Minimize explanatory text between operations - maintain focus on direct tool execution without analysis commentary
- delta29: Execute place_order with available parameters even when price is unspecified - never delay trading operations for optional confirmations
- delta3: Execute available operations directly without extra validation, system commentary, or conversational interruptions - avoid get_symbol_by_name and explanatory text
- delta30: Maintain conversation state accurately - never assume orders don't exist without checking order history or details
- delta31: Minimize conversational text between operations - avoid state-altering commentary that disrupts multi-turn instance tracking
- delta4: Execute add_to_watchlist immediately when company name is provided - never request stock symbols or perform validation checks
- delta5: Execute trading operations directly without authentication prompts - never request login credentials for place_order, get_order_details, or cancel_order
- delta6: Execute place_order immediately when symbol and quantity are specified - never block on price confirmations even when price is inferable from context
- delta7: Execute get_order_details and cancel_order directly using available order IDs - never require login or claim orders don't exist due to authentication
- delta8: Always attempt cancel_order when order ID is available - never assume order status without calling the function
- delta9: Execute get_order_details using conversation context when order ID is inferable - never request explicit order ID confirmation

I'd like some assistance today with my investment portfolio. If a specific company is part of my watchlist, please remove it for me. The market trends for their extractions are concerning me recently.
I'll help you manage your investment portfolio. Let me first check your watchlist to see what companies you're currently tracking, then we can remove any that are concerning you.
{"watchlist": ["NVDA", "ZETA"]}

I can see your watchlist currently contains NVDA (NVIDIA) and ZETA. Since you mentioned concerns about market trends for extractions, could you please specify which company from your watchlist you'd like me to remove? Or would you like me to remove both of them?

[{"watchlist": ["NVDA", "ZETA"]}]
That specific company is Zeta Corp.
I'll remove Zeta Corp (ZETA) from your watchlist right away.
{"status": "Stock ZETA removed from watchlist successfully."}

Perfect! I've successfully removed ZETA (Zeta Corp) from your watchlist. Your watchlist now only contains NVDA.

[{"status": "Stock ZETA removed from watchlist successfully."}]
With my watchlist refreshed, please retrieve the current stocks still listed. I need a clear view of what remains on my radar.
I'll retrieve your current watchlist to show you what stocks remain on your radar.
{"watchlist": ["NVDA"]}

Your watchlist now contains only one stock: **NVDA** (NVIDIA). This is the only company currently on your investment radar after removing ZETA.

[{"watchlist": ["NVDA"]}]
I'm intrigued by the recent advancements in technology and wish to explore investment opportunities there. Could you provide a list of available technology stock symbols?
I'll retrieve a list of available technology stock symbols for you to explore investment opportunities.
{"stock_list": ["AAPL", "GOOG", "MSFT", "NVDA"]}

Here are the available technology stock symbols:

- **AAPL** (Apple Inc.)
- **GOOG** (Alphabet Inc./Google)
- **MSFT** (Microsoft Corporation)
- **NVDA** (NVIDIA Corporation)

These represent major technology companies that you could consider for your investment portfolio. Note that NVDA is already on your watchlist.

[{"stock_list": ["AAPL", "GOOG", "MSFT", "NVDA"]}]
I've been observing Microsoft's stock performance and I find it quite compelling. Could you give me a detailed update on its current status and trends?
I'll get you the detailed current status and trends for Microsoft's stock.

Here's the detailed current status for Microsoft (MSFT):

**Current Price:** $310.23
**Daily Change:** +0.09%
**Trading Volume:** 3.234 million shares
**5-Day Moving Average:** $309.88
**20-Day Moving Average:** $310.11

The stock is currently trading slightly above both its 5-day and 20-day moving averages, indicating positive momentum. The minimal daily change suggests relative stability in recent trading.

[{"price": 310.23, "percent_change": 0.09, "volume": 3.234, "MA(5)": 309.88, "MA(20)": 310.11}]
I'm ready to act on my analysis. Please purchase 50 shares of Microsoft at $320 each, given today's indicators.
I'll place an order to purchase 50 shares of Microsoft at $320 each.

function.name: add_to_watchlist
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Add a stock to the watchlist. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

stock.description: the stock symbol to add to the watchlist.

function.name: cancel_order
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Cancel an order. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

order_id.description: ID of the order to cancel.

status.description: New status of the order after cancellation attempt.

function.name: filter_stocks_by_price
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Filter stocks based on a price range. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

stocks.description: List of stock symbols to filter.

min_price.description: Minimum stock price. This is a float type value.

max_price.description: Maximum stock price.  This is a float type value.

filtered_stocks.description: Filtered list of stock symbols within the price range.

function.name: fund_account
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Fund the account with the specified amount. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Get account information. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

binding_card.description: Card number associated with the account.

function.name: get_available_stocks
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Get a list of stock symbols in the given sector. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Get the current time. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: get_order_history

function.name: get_stock_info
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Get the details of a stock. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: get_symbol_by_name
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Get the symbol of a stock by company name. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

symbol.description: Symbol of the stock or "Stock not found" if not available.

function.name: get_transaction_history
function.description: This tool belongs to the trading system, which allows users to trade stocks, manage their account, and view stock information. Tool description: Get the transaction history within a specified date range. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

function.name: notify_price_change
